column3: BSB follows the critical text with “Christ Jesus” and “and in view of His appearing”; the Textus Receptus adds “therefore,” “the Lord,” and reads “at His appearing.”
BSB renders “with all patience and instruction” as “with every form of patient instruction.”
BSB adds “like a drink offering,” which the Greek verb implies.
BSB renders “having loved the present age” as “in his love of this world” and adds “has gone.”
BSB adds “my” and renders “the books” as “scrolls.”
BSB follows the critical text with “will repay” (ἀποδώσει); the Textus Receptus has the wish “may … repay.”
BSB renders “And I was delivered” as “So I was delivered.”
BSB follows the critical text: “The Lord” without “Jesus Christ,” and no “Amen.” The Textus Receptus also adds a closing note about writing from Rome.
